newsitem.title: CHINA: China firms urged to issue more short-term paper.
newsitem.headline: China firms urged to issue more short-term paper.

text.p: The Shanghai Securities News on Saturday urged state enterprises in the city to make greater use of short-term financial instruments to improve their cash flow.
The newspaper said firms in the city made use of 149 issues of short-term financial paper in 1996 with a total value of 1.679 billion yuan, about the same as the year before.
"Short-term financial instrument issues have provided much-needed relief of cash-flow troubles for 110 of the city's state enterprises," the newspaper said.
"Over time, more and more companies are seeing the positive benefits of the careful use of short-term financial instruments," it added.
It did not give details of the types of instruments issued by the state enterprises.
It said it was essential for enterprises to increase issues of financial papers to offset their debts.
